surface_mechanism_description: The ALD reaction between nickelocene and ozone involves the formation of a nickel-deﬁcient oxide Ni0.88O with the crystal structure of NiO. The stoichiometry can be adjusted by annealing under inert or aerobic conditions, where the partial pressure of O2 drives further oxidation.
evidence: The nickel-deﬁcient nature of the ﬁlm affects its magnetic properties. At room temperature, the sample gives rise to a diamagnetic signal (black squares of Fig. 3), most of which is due to the substrate. This behavior is consistent with either a diamagnetic ﬁlm or an antiferromagnetic one — the former case often being observed for bulk sub-stoichiometric oxide, whereas NiO notoriously has the latter character. Upon annealing under argon, however, the material is transformed. Changes in morphology and magnetism start to be discernible at 500 8C, and after an hour-long annealing at 700 8C they are complete. The ﬁlm continuity has been irreversibly lost and clusters of various sizes have formed (Fig. 2c). The material is thereby completely converted to metallic nickel, as shown by the GIXRD Communication. The evolution of O2 gas from the oxide upon thermal treatment in argon can be monitored. When a nickel oxide ﬁlm is covered by an additional 50 nm thick amorphous Al2O3 layer (by ALD), a cross-section of the sample obtained (upon a 700 8C anneal under inert gas), investigated using transmission electron microscopy (TEM), reveals two new layers (Fig. 4a). The ﬁrst is a void space between the nickel-containing layer and the substrate, as conﬁrmed by energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopic proﬁling (Fig. 4b). The second consists of what appears as bubbles at the interface with Al2O3. We attribute both to the build-up of O2 liberated from the sub-stoichiometric material. After treatment at 800 8C, the stress induced by liberating molecular oxygen is released, as microscopic ﬁlm pieces have peeled off of the underlying substrate. Finally, the stoichiometry of the nickel oxide initially grown can be changed by treating the ﬁlm at 700 8C without a protecting layer, under aerobic conditions. In this case, the partial pressure of O2 sufﬁces to maintain, and even increase, the O/Ni ratio in the solid. After cooling, the product contains 73% Ni by mass according to elemental analysis, which corresponds to Ni0.74O.
